Over the past two years, our production environment has consistently operated above 99.99% availability for all contracted clients, with no major unplanned outages exceeding 30 minutes. Our SLAs are designed so that, in practice, you won’t see material downtime attributable to us.

[Messages]
[System]: New message received from OrionSight Services Ltd. An automated summary is provided for convenience and may omit detail; please refer to full message and any attachments for binding content.

[Counterparty Representative]: Appreciate the clear proposal — it’s helpful to see your priorities laid out.

On commercials, $36,000/month for a 24-month firm term with extensive credits and a 90-day pilot at 50% fees is below where we can responsibly land for this scope. That said, we’re prepared to move meaningfully from our opening:
- Term: We can agree to a 36-month initial term with flexibility to discuss renewal options toward the end of year two. If you strongly prefer 24 months, we can explore that at a slightly higher rate.
- Price: We can reduce to $40,000/month for up to 120 endpoints on a 36-month term, or $41,500/month on a 24-month term.
- Pilot: We can support a 60-day pilot/early-service phase at 75% of the monthly fee, applied as a credit against the first contract year if you continue.

On SLA structure, our standard template (attached) includes:
- Defined uptime measurement on a calendar-month basis, excluding scheduled maintenance and force majeure
- A binding 30-minute initial response target for critical incidents with defined escalation paths
- Service credits that scale with actual downtime once monthly uptime for the contracted services falls below 99.95%

We’re comfortable adding language that clarifies data portability and basic exit assistance at no additional cost, provided that any bespoke tooling or heavy professional services are handled under a separate SOW.

Regarding evidence, we can share a current SOC 2 Type II report and a third-party uptime overview once we have an NDA in place. For proprietary reasons, we don’t typically provide raw redacted logs at this stage, but our existing clients in your segment can speak directly to their observed availability and our responsiveness.

If this revised framework is in range, I suggest we next align on the exact credit bands and renewal/termination language so we can both get internal approval.

[System]: Auto-summary of vendor counter: Vendor pushes back on your $36k/24-month/50% pilot proposal, offering instead $40k/month on a 36-month term (or $41.5k on 24 months), a 60-day pilot at 75% fees credited against year one if you proceed, and a standard SLA template with uptime measured monthly, exclusions, a 30-minute critical-response target, and service credits starting below 99.95% uptime. They agree in principle to data portability and basic exit assistance at no extra cost, and indicate they can share a SOC 2 Type II report and a third-party uptime overview under NDA, but not raw redacted logs.

[External Deal Coach]: This is a fairly typical pattern: you opened aggressively on both price and structure, and they’ve come back with a noticeable but not dramatic move.

A few points to consider:
- Dropping from $45k to $40k for the full scope over 36 months is a nontrivial concession, especially paired with a pilot at a discounted rate. It may not be your ideal number, but it’s within a range we often see for comparable deployments.
- The 60-day pilot at 75% is less generous than your ask, yet still gives you some real-world validation before you’re fully locked in, especially if paired with meaningful credits and clear termination conditions for repeated failures.
- They’re holding the credit trigger at 99.95% rather than the 99.99% headline. That’s negotiable: you might push for stronger credits closer to the marketing promise, or for additional remedies on chronic incident-response issues.

If you want to keep momentum, you could pick one or two areas to push harder on — for example, slightly better economics or more robust credits for serious downtime — while signaling flexibility elsewhere.
